newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden-Asia air cargo routes busy - market players.
newsitem.headline: Sweden-Asia air cargo routes busy - market players.

text.p: Ex-Sweden air cargo market players said on Monday capacity problems continued to plague Southeast Asian destinations, but on other routes the balance between supply and demand of cargo capacity seemed stable.
KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV regional director for the Nordic region Michael Steen said the airline had noted volumes which were better than last year.
"At this very moment there is a large amount for Southeast Asia. But we have not seen stagnation to any parts of the world," he told Reuters.
"The development is better than last year, and last year was a good year," he said.

The airline's cargo operations from Sweden are based at Skavsta airport in Nykoping, Sweden, 100 kms southwest of Stockholm. It flies around 300 tonnes capacity weekly on freighters from the Scandinavian country.
"We are looking into the possibility of adding capacity," said Steen, adding that the airline was pleased with its new operations from Skavsta which started in February.

Christer Carlsson, of the sales division of Swedish-based freight forwarder Air Cargo Express AB, said the company's most important routes continued to be the Far East, Australia, South America and Japan.
"For exports it's rather tight right now. But lately we have seen a slight drop in imports," Carlsson said, adding that it probably was because of a weaker crown.
The crown has softened from 4.41 against the mark on December 17 and from 4.34 in October. It was trading at 4.52 against the mark at midday on Monday.
Claes-Goran Amberfalt, of the Rock Drills shipping division at engineering group Atlas Copco, said capacity problems were only a concern for traffic to Japan.
"What we've seen in 1997 is that it seems we have the capacity we need. We suffered during 1996 to South America, but that has stabilised," he told Reuters.

"One market which is a problem today is Japan. For other markets that we use on a regular basis we don't have any major problems with capacity," said Amberfalt, adding that the United States, Canada and Australia were key destinations.
